In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
classical Cepheid stars are very good standard candles.
the new method is a useful and powerful tool to study the properties of pulsating stars, and it is a valuable complement to the classical methods.
, in spite of the many attempts to improve the classical Baade-Beck-Wesselink method, there is still no alternative that is as simple, reliable, and accurate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Baade-Wesselink method can now be considered a fully operational tool for the determination of distances and reddenings.
the Baade- Becker-Wesselink (BBW) method is now a powerful tool to determine the physical parameters of pulsating stars.
we can determine the color excess, intrinsic color and radius of a pulsating variable with an accuracy better than 0.01 mag, 0.02 mag, and 5%, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Baade- Becker-Wesselink relation is not a relation between two quantities, but a relation between four quantities.

the classical Cepheid distance scale, which has long been plagued by the uncertainties in the reddening estimates, is now firmly anchored in the open cluster distance scale, with a precision of better than 5% for the individual Cepheids considered.
the Baade- Becker-Wesselink approach can be used for the calibration of the period-luminosity relation of classical CepheIDs, and that this calibration is independent of the adopted reddening law.
